statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-45591 (GHSA-f8h2-vmm9-qhj6) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in the MessagePack hub protocol used by SignalR and Blazor Server: deeply nested MessagePack arrays cause a stack overflow. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, and Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.8 and fixed in 10.0.9 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f8h2-vmm9-qhj6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/405, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.9/10.0.9.md). For .NET 10 the fix updates the MessagePack reader that ASP.NET Core bundles and adds a test that parses 100,000 nested arrays (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/e3246058490de40dc0dfd381bb8904c115a3a67a, on the release/10.0.1xx branch, first in the v10.0.109 source release). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No package contains Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack.dll or its nupkg. The affected code ships in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll, which holds the Blazor Server MessagePack hub protocol and its MessagePack reader; in the 10.0.8-r0 aspnetcore10-runtime package it is the only assembly that contains the routines the fix removes. Each build holds four implementation copies of it on each architecture, all at the build's own .NET version: in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework of aspnetcore10-runtime, and in the shared framework of the .NET SDK, the ASP.NET Core runtime pack nupkg and the ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap. The other copies, in aspnetcore10-targeting-pack, dotnet10-runtime-artifacts and the SDK's reference pack, are reference assemblies with no implementation code. Extracted the aspnetcore10-runtime copy from every build on both architectures: The copies in the first 7 builds (10.0.2-r0 to 10.0.8-r0) contain the recursive TrySkipNextArray and TrySkipNextMap routines; from 10.0.9-r0 on, no copy contains them. In every build except the aarch64 10.0.2-r0 build, the implementation copies held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap have the same SHA-256 as the aspnetcore10-runtime copy; the aarch64 10.0.2-r0 bootstrap copies differ in bytes but carry the same 10.0.2 version and sit below the boundary. The range ends at 10.0.9-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-45591 (GHSA-f8h2-vmm9-qhj6) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in the MessagePack hub protocol used by SignalR and Blazor Server: deeply nested MessagePack arrays cause a stack overflow. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 9.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, and Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.16 and fixed in 9.0.17 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f8h2-vmm9-qhj6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/405, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.17/9.0.17.md). The fix patches the bundled MessagePack reader so it no longer skips nested values recursively (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/5edf41b9c09952f18e404ad38e25670991c1b513). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No package contains Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack.dll or its nupkg. The affected code ships in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll, which holds the Blazor Server MessagePack hub protocol and its MessagePack reader. Implementation copies are in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework carried by aspnetcore9-runtime and by the .NET SDK in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack nupkg that dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap also holds, and each carries the build's own .NET version; the other copies, in aspnetcore9-targeting-pack, dotnet9-runtime-artifacts and the SDK's reference pack, are reference assemblies with no implementation code. The copies in the first 5 builds (9.0.12-r0 to 9.0.16-r0) still contain the recursive TrySkipNextArray and TrySkipNextMap routines that the fix removes; from 9.0.17-r0 on no copy contains them. The range ends at 9.0.17-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
